## Preparing the example data

Hybrid imputation runs on log-transformed data after missingness
filtering, outlier removal, and `log1p()`
transformation. Here we prepare `log_transformed_df` from
`example_metabolomics`:

```{r setup}
library(OmicsProcessing)

data("example_metabolomics")
df <- example_metabolomics

filtered_df <- filter_by_missingness(
  df,
  row_thresh = 0.5,
  col_thresh = 0.5,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df$sample_type),
  filter_order = "iterative"
)

clean_df <- remove_outliers(
  filtered_df,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", filtered_df$sample_type),
  method = "pca-lof-overall",
  impute_method = "half-min-value",
  restore_missing_values = TRUE,
  return_ggplots = FALSE
)$df_filtered

log_transformed_df <- clean_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(tidyselect::contains("@"), log1p))

target_cols <- resolve_target_cols(log_transformed_df, "@")
sum(is.na(log_transformed_df[, target_cols]))
```

## Hybrid Imputation (Random Forest + LCMD)

```{r hybrid-imputation}
set.seed(42)

imputed_results <- hybrid_imputation(
  log_transformed_df,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", log_transformed_df$sample_type),
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  control_RF = list(verbose = FALSE)
)

imputed_df <- imputed_results$hybrid_rf_lcmd

# Inspect feature-level OOB errors and RF vs LCMD split
round(imputed_results$oob, 3)
table(method_used = ifelse(imputed_results$oob < 0.1, "RF", "LCMD"))
sum(is.na(imputed_df[, target_cols]))
```

`hybrid_imputation()` combines two complementary strategies:

* **Random Forest (RF)** via `missForest::missForest()` for features that
  are well-predicted by other variables (low OOBE).
* **Left-Censored Missing Data (LCMD)** via `imputeLCMD::impute.MAR.MNAR()`
  for features with higher OOBE.

The function fits RF per feature, uses the out-of-bag error (OOBE) to
decide whether to keep the RF estimate or switch that feature to LCMD,
and returns:

* `hybrid_rf_lcmd`: the combined result.
* `rf` / `lcmd`: per-method outputs.
* `oob`: OOBE values (helpful for diagnostics).

See the full reference: [`hybrid_imputation()`](../reference/hybrid_imputation.html).

### Handling QC samples with `is_qc`

Rows flagged as `TRUE` by `is_qc` are excluded from the hybrid imputation
calculations. The rationale is that QC samples are repeatedly measured
throughout the laboratory workflow and are intended to capture technical
variability in the measurement process. Excluding them prevents these rows
from influencing the RF and LCMD imputation models fitted to the biological
samples.

If QC samples contain missing values that you also want to impute, there
are two main options.

#### A. Impute QC samples together with the rest of the data

To include all rows in the hybrid imputation process, leave `is_qc` as
`NULL` (or pass `rep(FALSE, nrow(log_transformed_df))`):

```{r qc-all-together}
imputed_all <- hybrid_imputation(
  log_transformed_df,
  target_cols = "@",
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  is_qc = NULL,
  control_RF = list(verbose = FALSE)
)

sum(is.na(imputed_all$hybrid_rf_lcmd[, target_cols]))
```

#### B. Impute QC samples using only QC sample values

If you want to impute missing values in QC samples separately, using only
information from other QC samples, you can invert the `is_qc` vector.
This excludes all non-QC rows from the imputation calculations and
applies the pipeline only to the QC samples.

Since QC rows in `example_metabolomics` are complete, we introduce a few
missing values into QC rows below to demonstrate QC-only imputation:

```{r qc-only-imputation}
set.seed(1)
df_qc_missing <- log_transformed_df
qc_idx <- which(df_qc_missing$is_qc)
for (col in target_cols[1:5]) {
  df_qc_missing[sample(qc_idx, 3), col] <- NA_real_
}

sum(is.na(df_qc_missing[qc_idx, target_cols]))

imputed_qc_results <- hybrid_imputation(
  df_qc_missing,
  target_cols = "@",
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  is_qc = !df_qc_missing$is_qc,
  control_RF = list(verbose = FALSE)
)

imputed_qc_df <- imputed_qc_results$hybrid_rf_lcmd
sum(is.na(imputed_qc_df[qc_idx, target_cols]))
```

### Customising the RF and LCMD controls

You can tweak both engines via `control_RF` and `control_LCMD`:

```{r custom-controls}
my_control_RF <- list(
  parallelize = "no",
  mtry = floor(sqrt(length(target_cols))),
  ntree = 100,
  maxiter = 10,
  variablewise = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

my_control_LCMD <- list(
  method.MAR = "KNN",
  method.MNAR = "QRILC"
)

df_rf_lcmd_hybrid <- hybrid_imputation(
  log_transformed_df,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", log_transformed_df$sample_type),
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  control_LCMD = my_control_LCMD,
  control_RF = my_control_RF
)

sum(is.na(df_rf_lcmd_hybrid$hybrid_rf_lcmd[, target_cols]))
```

### Parallelising the RF step (`missForest`)

`run_rf_imputation()` manages cluster registration automatically when you
set `parallelize = "variables"` (or `"forests"`) and `n_cores` inside
`control_RF`:

```{r parallel-rf, eval = FALSE}
ctrl_parallel_RF <- list(
  parallelize = "variables", # or "forests"
  n_cores = 2,
  mtry = floor(sqrt(length(target_cols))),
  ntree = 200,
  maxiter = 10,
  variablewise = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

imputed_parallel <- hybrid_imputation(
  log_transformed_df,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", log_transformed_df$sample_type),
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  control_RF = ctrl_parallel_RF
)
```

Guidance:

* Use `parallelize = "variables"` for many features; `"forests"` spreads
  trees instead.
* Keep `ntree` reasonable when parallelising to avoid memory pressure.

Tips:

* Keep `target_cols` explicit when possible for clarity; `"@"` matches
  all `"mass@rt"` feature columns via `resolve_target_cols()`.
* Inspect `imputed_results$oob` to confirm the RF ↔ LCMD split aligns
  with your expectations.
* For very wide matrices, tune `ntree`, `mtry`, or `n_cores` to balance
  runtime and stability.
